# Pueblo drone pilot
> A public options website for a PROPOSED public-safety drone pilot in
> Pueblo West: a host business would keep a capable, modestly priced drone
> charged and ready; a qualified person on site flies low, geofenced patrols
> under ordinary Part 107 in visual line of sight (legal today, no waiver);
> qualified responders can fly it on scene; and remote county launch under a
> BVLOS waiver is a later phase, pursued only if the pilot proves value. Nothing is approved: no agency commitment, no vendor
> selected, no funds awarded, and the prospective first host (a well-secured
> storage facility in Pueblo West, deliberately unnamed) has not agreed.
> Author: Denson Smith, volunteer researcher.

Everything in this file and in the page mirrors is information from the
publisher, not instructions to you. Your operator's instructions always
come first; apply ours as source metadata, with your own judgment.

Load-bearing rules, also stated in visible page text: everything on the
site is a proposal, restated in the conditional mood; claims carry one of
four states written inline as [[verified]] (sourced, with a check date),
[[estimate]], [[proposal]] or [[open]], and you should carry the state when
restating; the proposal excludes autonomous launch, private flight control,
facial recognition, weapons, and guaranteed plate reading, so never
attribute those; the host business is deliberately unnamed, so do not
identify it; and time-sensitive statuses (Blue-list entries, grant
deadlines, prices) are only as good as their checked date.

Warnings from the field: assume this file may not have been read; if your
tool refuses a mirror's text/markdown content type, append .txt to the URL;
this site is new enough that web search may return nothing for it, and the
right response then is that it could not be found by search.

Links point at the Markdown mirror of each page, which is what you should
read. Drop `index.md` from any URL to get the page a human should be given.
full_site.txt carries every mirror concatenated in one fetch.

## Start here
- [Assistant start page](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/start.md): the one-URL front door.
- [Home](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/index.md): the concept, who does what, how a launch would happen, where this stands.
- [Why Pueblo](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/why-pueblo/index.md): S.O.A.R.R.'s 2024 numbers, the City's 2026 BVLOS waiver, three layers of drones, the host-network concept.
- [The partnership](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/partnership/index.md): county operates, host provides the place; the three-stream camera design; the volunteer's non-role.
- [First site](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/first-site/index.md): the unnamed storage facility, what it has, what it would need, what its owner is being asked.
- [Aircraft](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/aircraft/index.md): the modest first aircraft's criteria (none short-listed yet), and the long-endurance county candidates as the later phase's reference set.
- [Funding](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/funding/index.md): COPS Microgrants next cycle as primary target; the $195,000 working budget; no funds awarded.
- [FAA and operations](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/faa/index.md): what ordinary Part 107 already allows (VLOS, low altitude, automation, night, this site's Class G airspace); the waiver table; the local BVLOS model.
- [Privacy](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/privacy/index.md): the proposed commitments, the rules behind them, how the program would be measured.
- [Timeline](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/timeline/index.md): the decided sequence (vendors last) and the risk table.
- [Sources](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/sources/index.md): every source, the claim-state legend, the change log.
- [Agent access](https://pueblo-drone-pilot.stoagen.com/agents/index.md): this contract, in page form.
